title: Speech online
hook: the same rules apply to messages and posts
tomorrow: tara starts it again at lunch. what if simran says nothing?

segments.voice: Yesterday, forgiving someone: where there is forgiveness, there the Lord is. Simran deleted one reply. She's drafted a better one.

It's a good post. Simran has rewritten it four times: funny, cutting, nothing anyone could report. A photo of a candle, captioned: some of us are actually nice in real life. She and Maya are studying at Maya's grandma's kitchen table. Maya's grandma reads the screen over her glasses and quotes the Bible she keeps by the stove: Death and life are in the power of the tongue. Then she adds, and the thumbs too, these days.
screen: `A CANDLE, A CAPTION, A JAB.` → `MAYA'S GRANDMA READS IT.` → `DEATH AND LIFE, IN THE TONGUE.`

segments.voice: So, the question: does a post count as speech? Sikh teaching answers in Sheikh Farid's voice, in saloks kept in the Guru Granth Sahib. In paraphrase: don't speak even one harsh word, because the true Master lives in everyone. Don't break anyone's heart; every heart is a priceless jewel. There's no exception for screens. A reply under someone's photo lands in the same heart a spoken word would. The screen just lets you skip seeing their face. Maya's grandma was quoting Proverbs, in the King James Bible: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof. Two traditions, and something they share: words are never small. They build or they break, and they come back to the one who speaks. And one honest difference. Proverbs weighs speech by its fruit, what it grows in the speaker's own life. Farid weighs it by who is listening: a heart with the Master living in it. Two angles on the same tongue, neither one cancelling the other. Here's the line to tell a friend tonight: there's no one at the other end of a post who isn't a jewel. Simran deletes the candle. Then she sends Kiran a chemistry meme instead.
screen: `DOES A POST COUNT AS SPEECH?` · `FARID: EVERY HEART IS A JEWEL.` · `PROVERBS: DEATH AND LIFE, THE TONGUE.` · `SHARED, AND ONE HONEST DIFFERENCE.` · then, large: `KIND ONLINE.`

segments.voice: Hold your phone with the screen dark, and just look at it: a small thing that carries your words into a lot of hearts. Bring to mind one person whose message you could answer kindly, and the few words you'd use. Then set it face down and rest your hands for the sit.
Speech online. Posts, comments and replies: speech with the face hidden, landing in the same heart. Maanak means a jewel.
Kind online: every reader at the other end of a post is somebody's jewel. Catch you tomorrow.
